verdicts.quote: The consumer is an internal, licensed Lightning Experience user of the development org. Not Experience Cloud/community users, not Slack, not Salesforce mobile app, not an Agentforce/Einstein bot channel.
Sharing: n/a, the service touches no records. ... These three are recorded as not applicable because no Salesforce record is read or written (A-3); adding a record read later reopens them.
Field-level security: n/a. These three are recorded as not applicable because no Salesforce record is read or written (A-3)
Access is granted through one permission set, "Grok Bot User", assigned by an administrator. ... Key entry and configuration edits: administrators only ... Runtime users never see or edit them.
Conversation history lives only in the open page (browser memory). Nothing is saved in the org ... Two browser tabs or two users never affect each other's transcript (no shared state)
Callouts must happen before any DML in the transaction (platform rule); the bot service performs no DML.
verdicts.missing: The spec chooses a synchronous callout and never addresses trigger contexts or an asynchronous (Queueable/future) design.

verdicts.quote: It is never in source control, deployed metadata values, browser payloads, debug logs, error messages, or the admin-editable configuration.
per-callout timeout 1 ms–120,000 ms (default 10 s), cumulative 120 s per transaction, 100 callouts per transaction ... synchronous heap 6 MB, CPU 10,000 ms
Callouts are mockable in tests without the key. ... The Apex test suite runs to green with no network and no key (mock only).
the Named Credential points at `https://api.x.ai` ... Apex calls `callout:<NamedCredentialApiName>/v1/chat/completions`.
every turn completes or fails inside one synchronous request ... The browser-side wait for a Salesforce server action may be shorter than the 60 s default callout timeout; unverified.
verdicts.missing: The spec relies on the inline return the nuance warns against, and leaves open whether the browser-side wait is long enough. No asynchronous notification mechanism is chosen.

verdicts.quote: Retry ... same message resent with same history; no new bubble ... The server does not deduplicate; double submits are prevented client-side. ... No duplicated or crossed-over messages.

RATE_LIMITED | xAI HTTP 429 | "Grok is receiving too many requests right now. Please wait a moment and try again." ... No automatic retries. A failed turn is reported once; the user retries manually.

verdicts.missing: No stored conversation/turn record shape (role, text, status, timestamps, model id, usage counts) is defined, because the spec chooses not to store conversations.

Only the text the user typed in this chat (and Grok's earlier replies) plus the configured system prompt leave Salesforce; no record data, user name, email, org id, or session id is sent.

An admin can rotate the key or switch the model in Setup and the next chat turn uses it. ... an administrator can correlate a reported reference id to a log line when a trace flag was active.
verdicts.missing: No explicit org-wide off switch. Admins can see failed requests only through debug logs while a trace flag is active, so there is no deliberate failure view.

verdicts.quote: Each turn writes one debug-log line without any message or reply content ... Persistent usage/audit storage is out of scope (no object created).
verdicts.missing: There is no audit record of who asked what and what was answered, and no retention for one; the spec scopes this out.

verdicts.missing: How configuration and credentials differ between environments, scratch org vs sandbox, and the production code-coverage requirement are not stated; production deployment is simply excluded.
